title: The Chess Player Appears
next_chapter_hook: Cang Yutian's words exploded like thunder beside Chen Ji's ears. He clenched his fists tight—did the fourth path really exist? And what lay at the end of that path?

text.content: The void at the entrance of the ruins trembled slightly. The communication jade talisman in Su Qingyao's hand continued to quiver, and the fluctuation mixed with Chen Nian's aura made her brow furrow tightly. She instinctively stepped back half a pace, her gaze locked firmly onto the barely visible rift ahead. A suffocating pressure filled the air, as if some ancient being was awakening from slumber.

"This aura..." Su Qingyao's fingertips turned faintly pale. She could sense a power gathering that far exceeded her comprehension. It wasn't spiritual energy, nor law—it was something more fundamental, as if threads of destiny were being plucked by invisible hands. She gritted her teeth; the cultivation of Tianqing Sect's Inner Disciple Senior Fellow seemed pathetically inadequate in this moment.

The rift suddenly expanded, and a figure emerged slowly from nothingness. He was a middle-aged man in plain white robes, with an elegant and approachable face, yet his eyes concealed a terrifying depth. Each step he took rested upon the void, as if invisible stairs bore his weight. Cang Yutian—the name surfaced from Chen Ji's memories, now presented before Su Qingyao in an almost absurd manner.

dialogue.content: "Ten thousand years of preparation, three paths converging into one." Cang Yutian's voice was as gentle as a spring breeze, yet carried undeniable authority. "Su Qingyao, you've arrived at the perfect moment. The scenes ahead require a witness." His gaze passed over Su Qingyao and fixed upon a direction behind her—where Chen Ji emerged slowly from the darkness, his expression grimly terrible.

text.content: Chen Ji felt his heartbeat quicken; the Tianji Record Fragment within him trembled violently, as if encountering something that instinctively terrified it. He drew a deep breath and forced himself to remain composed. The "waste" Chen persona must not crumble, not yet. Yet his fingertips were already trembling within his sleeves—not from fear, but from fury.

dialogue.content: "Cang Yutian." Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm. "The strategist from ten thousand years ago, the puppet master behind the three great sects, the true source of the Tianji Record—am I correct?" His eyes locked onto his opponent as a faint smile curled his lips. "Never imagined I'd meet the real you today."

Cang Yutian clapped lightly, the sound crisp in the silent ruin entrance. "Excellent, excellent." A hint of appreciation gleamed in his gaze. "You truly haven't disappointed me. The three paths you deduced using the Tianji Record—the Demonic Path, Xuanwu, Tianqing—were all pieces I set in motion ten thousand years ago." He shook his head, a knowing smile crossing his face. "Chen Ji, your so-called rebellion is merely the third chapter of the script."

text.content: This sentence struck Chen Ji's heart like a heavy hammer. His breath caught abruptly as countless images flashed through his mind—those schemes he believed were his own meticulous plans, those choices he thought were his rebellious destiny... Had everything from the beginning been foreseen by this "chess player"? Rage surged through his chest like magma, and he felt the Tianji Record Fragment trembling violently within him.

choice.prompt: Facing Cang Yutian's mockery, Chen Ji had to make a choice:

choices.description: Directly confront Cang Yutian—even if you're the orchestrator, don't expect me to submit obediently. The Tianji Record belongs to me; I'll use it to carve my own bloody path!
choices.risk_hint: Might play directly into Cang Yutian's hands

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly raised his head, a sharp light flickering in his eyes. He wasn't blinded by rage; instead, he suppressed that power deep within his chest, fixing Cang Yutian with an almost challenging gaze. "A script?" A slow smile spread across his lips. "Since it's a script, then let me see—what ending does this script have?"

dialogue.content: "Interesting." Cang Yutian's eyes narrowed slightly. "In ten thousand years, you're the first to dare look at me this way. Truly worthy of being chosen by the Tianji Record—though only a fragment." He took a step forward, his oppressive aura suddenly intensifying. "But do you think knowing the truth can change anything?"

text.content: Chen Ji felt a burning sensation in his chest—that was the Tianji Record Fragment responding to his emotions. Some long-dormant power was awakening within him, like a lurking beast finally opening its eyes. He knew the true awakening was about to begin.

choices.description: Suppress the rage and analyze Cang Yutian's words with the calmest mind for weaknesses. Why would a strategist from ten thousand years ago reveal himself at this moment? There must be a variable he cannot ignore.
choices.risk_hint: Cang Yutian might see through your intentions

text.content: Chen Ji drew a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the surging fury in his chest. His eyes returned to their usual composure, even carrying a hint of gentle smile. "Cang Yutian senior speaks truly." He slightly cupped his hands, his posture humble as if facing an esteemed elder. "The junior indeed is merely a piece. But may I ask, senior—if everything lies within your control, why have you personally appeared?"

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian's steps faltered slightly. His gaze toward Chen Ji held a deeper scrutiny, seemingly surprised by this young man's composure. "You're quite clever." He spoke slowly, "Indeed, my reason for appearing is simple—because your existence has disrupted the original balance." His tone finally carried a hint of seriousness, "The Tianji Record chose you, and that itself is a variable I've never witnessed in ten thousand years."

text.content: Su Qingyao listened nearby, her heart pounding with fear. She finally understood Chen Ji's intention—not reckless counterattack, but precise probing. Cang Yutian's appearance itself was a flaw; a chess player who had been laying plans for ten thousand years would never expose himself so easily. His choice to appear at this moment indicated that Chen Ji's existence had already touched his bottom line.

choices.description: Acknowledge being a chess piece, even proactively showing weakness. Cang Yutian wants to see his reaction, so he'll perform for him. The true killing move must be reserved for the end.
choices.risk_hint: Cang Yutian May Have Another Trial

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes instantly dimmed, his shoulders slumping slightly, his entire being emanating a sense of dejection. "The senior is right." His voice was hoarse, "This junior is merely a piece of waste, fortunate enough to obtain the Tianji Record Fragment, and presumptuously believing I could reverse my fate. Now it seems, it's merely a joke." He slowly knelt, bowing to Cang Yutian with an almost humble posture.

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian watched Chen Ji kneeling on the ground silently, his eyes showing no ripples. "Is this your choice?" His voice carried a hint of imperceptible disappointment, "Could the one chosen by the Tianji Record surrender so easily?" He shook his head, "It seems I overestimated you." He turned, seemingly about to retreat into nothingness again.

Su Qingyao bit her lower lip hard. She knew Chen Ji was acting, but she wasn't sure if this play could deceive this unfathomable presence before her. Her hand quietly gripped her sword hilt, ready to strike at any moment—even knowing she was no match, she would fight for Chen Ji to grasp a sliver of chance.

text.content: Cang Yutian turned back, gazing into Chen Ji's eyes as if to see through all his secrets. After a moment, he sighed lightly. "Enough. No matter which path you choose, it's all within my expectations." He raised his hand, and an arcane rune condensed in his palm. "But there is something I must let you know—the Tianji Record is not my creation; I am merely its guardian. Ten thousand years ago, I was ordered to guard this divine artifact, waiting for the truly destined one."

Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, a flash of shock in his eyes. The Tianji Record was not Cang Yutian's creation? Then what was its true origin? "Ordered?" He caught the key word, "Whose orders are you following?" "This question—" Cang Yutian's voice suddenly grew low, "When you truly awaken one day, you will naturally know." His gaze shifted toward the depths of the ruins, "But before that, you need to make a choice."

dialogue.content: "Three paths are all my arrangements." Cang Yutian spoke slowly, "Tianqing Sect, Xuanwu Sect, Holy Sect of the Demonic Path—each choice seems to give you freedom, but in reality, all are under my guidance. But now—" He paused, a meaningful light flickering in his eyes, "I offer you the fourth path." Chen Ji's heart rate suddenly accelerated. The Tianji Record Fragment within him vibrated intensely, as if sensing some crucial turning point.

choice.prompt: Facing Cang Yutian's proposal of the "Fourth Path," how should Chen Ji respond:

choices.text: Press for What the Fourth Path Is
choices.description: Since Cang Yutian proactively proposed this, it's a flaw in his arrangement. Press him directly to force him to reveal more truth.
choices.risk_hint: Cang Yutian May Be Setting a Trap

text.content: "The fourth path?" Chen Ji's voice tightened slightly, but he quickly stabilized his emotions, "Since the senior has brought it up, I presume you wouldn't mind elaborating." His eyes stared directly at Cang Yutian, "I'm curious—what kind of way out would a plotter from ten thousand years ago offer a chess piece?"

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian chuckled lightly, the laughter carrying a mix of appreciation and playfulness. "Impatient." He shook his head, "The fourth path is neither a smooth road nor a shortcut. It's a path no one has ever walked—no script, no predetermined ending." His gaze deepened, "The true fourth path requires you to write it yourself."

text.content: These words struck like thunder in Chen Ji's mind. "Write it yourself"—these four words directly hit the core essence of the Tianji Record. He suddenly realized that he had been using the Tianji Record's power all along but never truly mastered it. Fate Writing—this was the true secret of the Tianji Record!

choices.description: Why would someone who has been plotting for ten thousand years kindly offer him a fourth path? There must be some ulterior motive hidden in this.

text.content: Chen Ji did not rush to respond, but quietly stared at Cang Yutian. His gaze gradually sharpened, as if examining a cunning fox. "Elder, you have been setting up this board for ten thousand years, all just to wait for a chess piece to awaken?" His voice was soft, yet carried a bone-penetrating chill. "Forgive my bluntness—but what you desire is probably not an awakened Tianji Record holder, but a more obedient chess piece, correct?"

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian's smile faltered slightly. For the first time, genuine surprise flickered in his eyes when he looked at Chen Ji. "You are smarter than I imagined." He spoke slowly. "But you are wrong about one thing—I do not wish to control you, but to guide you." His voice lowered. "Because once the power of the Tianji Record goes out of control, what would be destroyed is not just this continent, but... what I have protected for ten thousand years."

text.content: Su Qingyao listened from the side, her heart leaping in terror. She finally understood Cang Yutian's true purpose—not to destroy the Tianji Record, but to prevent it from running amok. But where exactly was the line between "guidance" and "control"? She unconsciously gripped her sword hilt, her gaze shifting back and forth between Chen Ji and Cang Yutian.

choices.description: Since Cang Yutian has something he desires, terms can be negotiated. Use the chips in hand to exchange for more information about his sister Chen Nian.
choices.risk_hint: Cang Yutian Might Use This as Leverage

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, suppressing the churning emotions in his chest, and restored his usual humility as a废物 disciple. "Since the Elder has proposed this fourth path, the junior is deeply grateful." He slightly cupped his hands. "But there is one request the junior must make—my sister Chen Nian was taken away by the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path many years ago. Since the Elder knows everything about the Tianji Record, surely you also know her whereabouts?"

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian's eyes flickered subtly. "Chen Nian, the Heavenly Fate Lock Key." He spoke this name slowly. "You are indeed making clever calculations." His gaze became profound. "I can tell you her whereabouts—but the price is, you must complete one of these three paths. As the grand finale of my chess game." He smiled faintly. "Rest assured, I will not force you. Choose one of the three paths. After you complete it, I will naturally tell you where Chen Nian is."

text.content: All three paths were Cang Yutian's arrangements. No matter which one he chose, he would remain within the other's control. But if he chose none, he would never know his sister's whereabouts... Chen Ji felt a suffocating pressure. He finally realized the terrifying aspect of this ten-thousand-year chess player—not only did he control the overall situation, but he also knew how to exploit what his opponents cared about most.

Just then, the Tianji Record Fragment within Chen Ji's body suddenly trembled violently, and a scorching force spread from his chest, surging directly into his Mental Sea. Cang Yutian's eyes narrowed abruptly, as if sensing something. For the first time, his expression underwent a noticeable change—that was surprise, wariness, and an indescribable anticipation.

"You—" Cang Yutian took a step forward, his gaze firmly locked on Chen Ji. "The Tianji Record is responding to you." His voice carried a note of disbelief. "For ten thousand years, it has never actively responded to anyone, not even those self-proclaimed Heavenly Favorees. But you—a废物 disciple—actually让它主动觉醒?" He took a deep breath, his wariness gradually being replaced by an almost fanatical light. "It seems the variable I have waited ten thousand years for has finally appeared."

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian threw his head back and laughed wildly, the laughter carrying a hint of madness and relief. "Good! Good! Good!" He said three "goods" in succession. "Chen Ji, you truly have not disappointed me!" His figure began to grow illusory, as if about to sink back into the void. "Since the Tianji Record has chosen you, I shall give you a chance—a real chance. The next volume of the chess game, you shall play the pieces yourself.届时，我会再来找你."

choice.prompt: Facing the Departing Cang Yutian, Chen Ji Made His Final Choice:

choices.description: Cang Yutian wants to leave whenever he pleases? Not so fast! Leave harsh words, letting him know that someday he will be retaliated against.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, his eyes burning with unyielding fire. "Cang Yutian!" His voice was like metal striking stone, carrying undeniable resolve. "Today's favor, Chen Ji will forever engrave in his heart!" The corner of his lips slowly lifted, revealing a cold smile. "The next time we meet, this chess game—it should be my turn to play the pieces!"

Cang Yutian's figure slightly paused. He turned his head, his gaze toward Chen Ji carrying a bit more scrutiny and... appreciation. "Bold." he said softly. "In ten thousand years, you are the second person who dares to say such words to me." His form completely dissolved into nothingness, leaving only a voice echoing in the air. "I await you."

text.content: Su Qingyao stared blankly at this scene, her heart churning with indescribable emotions. The "废物 junior brother" she had been secretly observing all along, the气魄and胆量 he displayed at this moment even made the ten-thousand-year chess player take notice. Her heartbeat unconsciously accelerated—was this the true Chen Ji?

choices.description: Leaving no evidence. Cang Yutian was probing, so he responded with silence. Let him guess about the next move.
choices.risk_hint: Missed the chance to state his position

text.content: Chen Ji said nothing. He simply stood there quietly, his gaze calm as he watched Cang Yutian's figure fade away. No harsh words, no anger, not even an expression. His silence itself was an answer. Cang Yutian's final words lingered in the air: "Next time we meet, this chess game—it shall be my turn to be the Chess Player!"

Su Qingyao walked to Chen Ji's side and asked softly, "Are you alright?" Her gaze carried a hint of worry. "That person... was terrifying. I've never felt such overwhelming pressure." She paused, then added, "And about your sister's matter... I'll help you." Chen Ji turned to look at her, a complex light flickering in his eyes. This woman who had been secretly investigating him had now chosen to stand by his side.

"Let's go." Chen Ji said softly. "This place isn't safe to linger." His eyes swept across the depths of the ruins, where perhaps more secrets awaited discovery. But now was not the time for exploration—he needed time to process everything that had transpired. The Tianji Record quivered gently within him, as if speaking of something. He faintly sensed that the true awakening... had only just begun.

The void at the ruins entrance was completely restored to tranquility. Cang Yutian's figure had long since dissipated into the void, leaving only that chilling pressure gradually fading from the air. Su Qingyao let out a long breath, her palms damp with sweat. The confrontation just now, though lasting only a brief incense stick's time, had made her feel as if she'd survived a life-and-death ordeal.

"Chen Ji." Su Qingyao's voice was somewhat hoarse. "Have you... always been like this?" She looked at the young man beside her, her gaze carrying a complex mixture of unfamiliarity and familiarity intertwined. The usually cowardly and卑微 waste of a junior brother had displayed such spirit and courage in the刚才的对峙 that even she, the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, felt ashamed. She suddenly understood why the Tianji Record had chosen him—this seemingly ordinary young man had inscribed in his bones defiance and pride.

Chen Ji did not answer her question. His gaze turned toward the distant horizon, toward the direction of the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path. His sister Chen Nian's whereabouts, Cang Yutian's truth, the ultimate secrets of the Tianji Record... all clues pointed in the same direction. He clenched his fists tightly, his knuckles whitening from the force. Heavenly Fate circulated within his body, the just-awakened power taking root and flourishing within him.

dialogue.content: "Senior Sister Su." Chen Ji suddenly spoke, his voice soft yet carrying undeniable resolve. "There are things I cannot tell you yet. But please believe—everything I do has its reason." He turned his head,直视 Su Qingyao's eyes. "When this is over, I will give you a complete answer." His eyes were deep as an abyss, as if hiding countless secrets. "Before that—" His lips curved slightly upward. "Please continue playing the role of the person 'secretly investigating me.'"

text.content: Su Qingyao stared at him, her heart churning with countless emotions. She wanted to ask, wanted to investigate, but ultimately could only nod gently. "Alright." Her voice was soft. "I'll wait for you." She turned and walked toward the depths of the ruins, but after several steps she stopped and glanced back at Chen Ji. "Chen Ji, remember—no matter what happens, Su Qingyao, Inner Disciple Senior Fellow of Tianqing Sect, will always stand on your side." With that, her figure vanished into the darkness of the ruins.

Chen Ji stood alone at the ruins entrance, the night wind brushing against his robe with a chill. He retrieved the Tianji Record Fragment from his chest. The ancient bamboo slip shimmered with a faint, ethereal glow under the moonlight. He gazed at the text on the fragment, Cang Yutian's parting words echoing in his mind—"The true fourth path must be written by yourself." Fate's inscription, ten thousand years of change. He carefully secured the fragment, his expression hardening with unprecedented resolve. The chess game had begun, and he would ultimately become the Chess Player.
